Compute the terms of each topic

Source: R/terms.R
terms.sbert_topic_model.Rd

terms() computes the ranked terms of each topic of a fitted model: the words that distinguish its texts from the texts of the other topics. Class-based TF-IDF (Grootendorst 2022) treats all the texts of a topic as one document and weights each term by its frequency in the topic against its frequency across all topics, so that a word frequent everywhere ranks low and a word frequent in one topic ranks high.

The terms describe a topic in words and complement its representative texts. They depend only on the topic assignments and the text, so terms() recomputes them under any term settings: changing the weighting, the stop words, the number filters, or stemming does not refit the model or encode anything. Every argument left NULL keeps the value the model was fitted with. Besides the weight (score), each term has its frequency in the topic and its probability within the topic (beta), and sort_by = "beta" ranks the words a topic uses most rather than the most distinctive ones. The result is a data frame with one row per topic and term.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sbert_topic_model'
terms(
  x,
  n = NULL,
  stop_words = NULL,
  min_term_frequency = NULL,
  min_token_length = NULL,
  weighting = NULL,
  reduce_frequent_words = NULL,
  stem = NULL,
  numbers = NULL,
  roman_numerals = NULL,
  section_numbers = NULL,
  smoothing = 0,
  sort_by = c("score", "beta"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A topic model fitted by topics().

n

Terms per topic; NULL (default) uses the model's n_terms.

stop_words

Words excluded from the terms; NULL (default) uses the model's list. See stop_words().

min_term_frequency

Minimum corpus-wide frequency of a term.

min_token_length

Minimum length of a term, in characters.

weighting

Term weighting: "ctfidf" or "bm25".

reduce_frequent_words

Whether to take the square root of within-topic frequencies before weighting.

stem

Whether to merge inflected forms under one Porter stem (needs the SnowballC package).

numbers, roman_numerals, section_numbers

Whether to "keep" or "remove" digit-only tokens, Roman-numeral tokens, and section or list numbering.

smoothing

Additive smoothing of beta (default 0). With 0, each topic's beta over its terms sums to one; a positive value reserves probability for the terms a topic does not use.

sort_by

Order of the terms within a topic: "score" (default), the class-based weight, or "beta", the probability within the topic. n is applied after ordering.

...

Ignored.

Value

A base data frame with one row per topic and term, and columns topic, label, term, rank, score (the class-based weight), frequency (count within the topic), and beta (the probability of the term within the topic).

Conditions

An error of class sbert_no_terms when no term passes the filters, and sbert_missing_package for stem = TRUE without SnowballC.

References

Grootendorst, M. (2022). BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure. arXiv:2203.05794.

Mendonca, M. and Figueira, A. (2025). Modeling political discourse with Sentence-BERT and BERTopic. arXiv:2510.22904.

See also

topics(); keywords() for the keywords of single documents; coherence() and topic_diversity(), which evaluate the terms; plot() with type = "terms".

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
terms(topic_model, n = 3)
